bill_title: Midnight Rules Relief Act
aflcio_description: This bill would allow Congress to combine into one resolution of disapproval all rules finalized by federal agencies near the end of a presidential term. The legislation would permit Congress to overturn in one fell swoop countless regulations that can take years, if not decades, to develop, stripping away vital protections from workers and the public. The bill passed the House without amendment.

bill_title: Regulations from the Executive in Need of Scrutiny (REINS) Act
aflcio_description: This bill would radically alter the regulatory process by requiring Congress to approve all major rules before they can go into effect. Under the REINS Act, politics, not scientific judgement or agency expertise would dictate all regulatory actions. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Regulatory Accountability Act
aflcio_description: This bill would upend 40 years of labor, health safety and environmental laws by requiring agencies to adopt the cheapest rules, rather than those deemed most effective. This anti-regulatory bill would make protecting workers and the public secondary to limiting cost and impacts on businesses and corporations. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: FY2017 Budget Resolution
aflcio_description: A concurrent budget resolution that paves the way for a vote to repeal the Affordable Care Act under a procedure known as "reconciliation." Budget reconciliation rules allow for the expedited consideration of legislation and a simple majority for passage in the U.S. Senate. The measure passed the Senate and House without amendment.

bill_title: Resolution Overturning the Fair Pay and Safe Workplace Rule
aflcio_description: This resolution of disapproval overturned an Obama administration rule that would have required companies bidding on federal contracts to disclose past violations of labor and employment laws, including the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the Fair Labor Standards Act and the National Labor Relations Act. The resolution passed the House and Senate, was signed by President Trump and became law on March 27, 2017.

bill_title: Resolution Overturning the Retirement Plan Safe Harbor Rule
aflcio_description: This resolution of disapproval overturned an Obama administration rule that would have allowed states to create retirement programs for private sector workers whose employers do not offer any retirement savings plan. The resolution passed the House and Senate, was signed by President Trump and became law on April 13, 2017.

bill_title: SCRUB Act of 2017
aflcio_description: This bill, part of a broad anti-regulation agenda, would require any agency that issues a new regulation to remove an existing regulation of equal or greater cost. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Resolution Overturning the OSHA Injury and Illness Reporting Rule
aflcio_description: This resolution of disapproval overturned an Obama administration rule that would require employers to keep accurate and complete records of serious work-related injuries and illnesses for at least five years. The resolution passed the House and Senate, was signed by President Trump and became law on April 3, 2017.

bill_title: Regulatory Integrity Act of 2017
aflcio_description: The legislation strictly prohibits agencies from issuing "public communications" that "emphasize the importance" of a particular agency action unless the communication has the "clear purpose of informing the public of the substance or status" of the particular action. This bill would significantly undermine federal agencies' ability to engage and inform the public in a meaningful and transparent way. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Fairness in Class Action Litigation and Furthering Asbestos Claim Transparency Act
aflcio_description: This legislation would invade the privacy of asbestos victims by posting personal exposure and medical information online and create new barriers to victims receiving compensation for asbestos disease. It would give unfettered access to employers, insurance companies, workers compensation carriers and others who could use this information for any purpose including blacklisting workers from employment and fighting compensation claims. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: VA Accountability First Act
aflcio_description: This bill would dramatically weaken due process rights for frontline VA employees by lowering the standard of proof for disciplinary actions and shortening the period for workers to appeal dismissals and other adverse actions. The bill would supersede both the collective bargaining agreement between the VA and its unions and existing civil service protections. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Small Business Health Fairness Act
aflcio_description: This bill would allow for the establishment of association health plans that would be shielded from state regulation and allowed to sell coverage across state lines. Insurers would be permitted to sell bare-bones health plans, which would lead to market segmentation and higher premiums for plans with more comprehensive coverage. In addition, association health plans have a long history of insolvencies that have left consumers liable for millions of dollars in health care expenses. The legislation lacks adequate safeguards to protect against future insolvencies. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Register of Copyrights Selection and Accountability Act
aflcio_description: Artists, writers and filmmakers rely on copyright protections to ensure they are compensated fairly, and there are more than 5.5 million workers engaged in creative work. By making the head of the U.S. Copyrights Office a presidential appointee, confirmed by the U.S. Senate, the bill would strengthen the independence of the Copyright Office, and it would give the American people the opportunity to weigh in on the selection process through their elected representatives. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Working Families Flexibility Act

aflcio_description: This bill would allow employers to substitute comp time for overtime pay, reducing the take home pay of millions of workers and resulting in longer hours and more unpredictable schedules. Contrary to the bill’s title, employers would remain in charge of when workers could take their comp time. The bill would encourage employers to demand excessive hours and would create a cost advantage for businesses that would no longer pay cash overtime. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: American Health Care Act
aflcio_description: This bill would roll back Affordable Care Act coverage expansions and sharply reduce funding for the Medicaid program, taking health coverage away from 23 million people. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Department of Veterans Affairs Accountability and Whistleblower Protection Act
aflcio_description: This bill undercuts collective bargaining and civil service protections for Department of Veterans Affairs employees by weakening standards for discharges and even permitting the forfeiture of some employees’ pensions. The bill passed the House and Senate, was signed by President Trump and became law on June 23, 2017.

bill_title: No Sanctuary for Criminals Act
aflcio_description: This bill would cut off federal funds to jurisdictions that limit its cooperation with federal immigration enforcement agents in order to protect low-priority immigrants from deportation, while still turning over those who have committed serious crimes. The bill would punish “sanctuary cities” that commit to engage in sensible local policing and that work to end discrimination and racial profiling by withholding federal funding for critical public safety programs. The bill passed the House without amendment.

bill_title: Kate's Law
aflcio_description: This bill would increase penalties for civil violations of our immigration laws, putting tens of thousands more people behind bars at enormous cost to taxpayers. The bill passed the House without amendment.

bill_title: Amendment to Expedite Military Base Realignments and Closures
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Tom McClintock (R-Calif.) to the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018 (H.R. 2810) would have removed a provision that prohibits the formation of a federal commission that could order an expedited realignment and closing of military bases. While presenting a potential risk to our military readiness, previous recommendations resulted in closings that did not produce the long-term savings that were expected. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Amendment to Repeal Prevailing Wage Laws
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Paul Gosar (R-Ariz.) to the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018 (H.R. 2810) would have repealed Davis-Bacon coverage for projects funded under this bill. The Davis-Bacon Act requires companies to pay construction workers locally prevailing wages on federally funded projects. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Resolution Overturning Forced Arbitration Ban
aflcio_description: This resolution of disapproval overturned a rule adopted by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to ban the use of forced arbitration clauses. Forced arbitration clauses are the 'fine print' in contracts that force consumers to give up their right to sue and instead require disputes be resolved though individual arbitration. The resolution passed the House and Senate, was signed by President Trump and became law on Nov. 1, 2017.

bill_title: Amendment to Repeal Prevailing Wage Laws
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Steve King (R-Iowa) to the Make America Secure Appropriations Act, 2018 (H.R. 3219) would have repealed Davis-Bacon coverage for projects funded under this bill. The Davis-Bacon Act requires companies to pay construction workers locally prevailing wages on federally funded projects. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Amendment Prohibiting the Outsourcing of Federal Civilian Jobs
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Matt Cartwright (D-Penn.) to the Make America Secure Appropriations Act, 2018 (H.R. 3219) retains the longstanding ban on outsourcing federal civilian jobs at the Department of Defense using the discredited A-76 method. Both the Government Accountability Office and the Department of Defense Inspector General have concluded that the A-76 process is deeply flawed, disruptive and costly to agency missions. The amendment passed.

bill_title: Amendment to Repeal Prevailing Wage Laws
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Steve King (R-Iowa) to the Make America Secure and Prosperous Appropriations Act, 2018 (H.R. 3354) would have repealed Davis-Bacon coverage for Department of Transportation projects funded under this bill. The Davis-Bacon Act requires companies to pay construction workers locally prevailing wages on federally funded projects. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Amendment to Cut Funds for the Essential Air Service Program

Tom McClintock (R-Calif.) to the Make America Secure and Prosperous Appropriations Act, 2018 (H.R. 3354) would have eliminated funding for the Essential Air Service program, a critical program that provides access to air travel for small and rural communities. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Amendment to Eliminate Funds for the Gateway Rail Project
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Ted Budd (R-N.C.) to the Make America Secure and Prosperous Appropriations Act, 2018 (H.R. 3354) would have eliminated a $900 million allocation for the Gateway Rail Project. The project will provide critical improvements to aging and damaged Amtrak rail infrastructure, increase capacity and improve service reliability throughout the Northeast corridor. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Amendment to Defund Amtrak
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Mo Brooks (R-Ala.) to the Make America Secure and Prosperous Appropriations Act, 2018 (H.R. 3354) would have eliminated funding for Amtrak’s national rail network, a vital transportation link for millions of people, supports thousands of good paying jobs and provides enormous economic benefits across the nation. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Amendment to Repeal Prevailing Wage Laws
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Steve King (R-Iowa) to the Make America Secure and Prosperous Appropriations Act, 2018 (H.R. 3354) would have repealed Davis-Bacon coverage for Department of Interior projects funded under this bill. The Davis-Bacon Act requires companies to pay construction workers locally prevailing wages on federally funded projects. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Amendment to Repeal Prevailing Wage Laws
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Steve King (R-Iowa) to the Make America Secure and Prosperous Appropriations Act, 2018 (H.R. 3354) would have repealed Davis-Bacon coverage for Department of Homeland Security projects funded under this bill. The Davis-Bacon Act requires companies to pay construction workers locally prevailing wages on federally funded projects. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Amendment to Cut the National Labor Relations Board Budget
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Glenn Grothman (R-Wisc.) to the Make America Secure and Prosperous Appropriations Act, 2018 (H.R. 3354) would have cut the existing budget of the National Labor Relations Board from $274 million by $99 million. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Amendment to Cut Funding at the Mine Safety and Health Administration
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Mark Meadows (R-N.C.) to the Make America Secure and Prosperous Appropriations Act, 2018 (H.R. 3354) would have cut the budget of the Mine Safety and Health Administration by an additional ten percent. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Amendment to Repeal the NLRB Election Modernization Rule
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Tim Walberg (R-Mich.) to the Make America Secure and Prosperous Appropriations Act, 2018 (H.R. 3354) prevented funding to implement new procedures adopted by the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) in 2015 that streamlines representation elections and reduces employer interference. The amendment passed, repealing the NLRB election rule.

bill_title: Amendment to Repeal OSHA's Improved Injury Reporting Rules
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Bob Gibbs (R-Ohio) to the Make America Secure and Prosperous Appropriations Act, 2018 (H.R. 3354) prevented funding to implement modernized rules adopted by the Office of Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) in 2016 that updated injury reporting requirements and strengthened anti-retaliation protections. The amendment passed, repealing the modernized OSHA injury reporting rule.

bill_title: FY2018 Budget Resolution
aflcio_description: This resolution establishing the congressional budget for FY2018 cuts programs like Medicare, Medicaid and other income security programs that provide critical support to our nation's most vulnerable population by $4.1 trillion over the next decade to pay for trillions of dollars in tax giveaways for millionaires and major corporations. The fiscal blueprint would also cut discretionary spending, including funding for education, infrastructure, job training, housing assistance and financial aid for college students by $800 billion. By 2027, spending on domestic priorities as a share of the economy would be the lowest it has been since the Hoover Administration. The House agreed to the Senate amended budget resolution without amendment.

bill_title: CHAMPIONING HEALTHY KIDS Act
aflcio_description: While this bill would extend funding for programs such as the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) and community health centers, it would also impose damaging funding cuts to other essential health care programs, such as the Prevention and Public Health Fund, and reduces health coverage under the Affordable Care Act. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Save Local Business Act
aflcio_description: Browning-Ferris Industries, a case that clarified the right of workers to bargain with two employers who exercise joint control over the workplace. Moreover, the bill would establish a new, extremely narrow statutory definition of joint employer under both the National Labor Relations Act and the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: FY2018 Budget Act Amending the Tax Code to Reduce Tax Rates
aflcio_description: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code in a way that makes working people pay the price for massive tax giveaways to millionaires and wealthy corporations. In addition to lowering the top tax rate for wealthy individuals and reducing the corporate rate by nearly 40%, the bill lowers the tax rate on offshore profits to zero, which gives corporations a giant incentive to move American jobs offshore. The bill also eliminates the Affordable Care Act's individual mandate, which will mean the loss of health care for 13 million Americans and a 10% premium increase, on average. The bill passed the House and Senate, was signed by President Trump and became law on December 22, 2017.

bill_title: Corporate Governance Reform and Transparency Act
aflcio_description: This bill would make it more difficult for shareholders to receive impartial advice prior to voting on management proposals. It would redefine the term 'proxy advisory firm,' open up the research process to include lobbying by special interests and make it more difficult for shareholders to hold corporate management accountable. The bill passed the House.
